subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A particle moving along a straight line has the relation S = t³ + 2t + 3 connecting the distance S described by the particle in time t. Find the velocity and the acceleration of the particle at t = 4 sec.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how velocity and acceleration come from S, and where the 4 goes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate for velocity and acceleration
steps.margin_note: First mark. This is a rectilinear motion question. Differentiate twice before putting any number in: S to v, then v to a. The constant 3 disappears at the first differentiation and the +2 at the second.
steps.memory_tip: S, then v, then a — one differentiation at each arrow, always in that order.
lines: This is a rectilinear motion question. Velocity v = dS/dt and acceleration a = dv/dt.

recall.must_convey: That v = dS/dt = 3t² + 2 and a = dv/dt = 6t.
accept: velocity is the first derivative and acceleration is the second
differentiate S to get three t squared plus two
differentiate again to get six t
S ni differentiate cheste three t squared plus two vasthundi
v is d S by d t and a is d v by d t

steps.why: Both answers come from the same relation, so differentiating twice first and substituting afterwards is shorter and safer than substituting into S.
common_mistakes: Substituting t = 4 into S, which gives the distance 75 and not a velocity.
Differentiating only once and calling 3t² + 2 the acceleration.

steps.label: Substitute t = 4
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both values are wanted, so write both. The stem does not print a unit for S; metres and seconds are the standard reading, so velocity is m/sec and acceleration is m/sec². Use whatever unit the question paper prints.
steps.memory_tip: One substitution into each expression: 4 goes into v, then the same 4 goes into a.

lines.text: ∴ at t = 4 sec, velocity = 50 m/sec and acceleration = 24 m/sec²

recall.must_convey: That at t = 4 the velocity is 50 and the acceleration is 24.

common_mistakes: Answering only the velocity and leaving out the acceleration.
Giving the acceleration in m/sec instead of m/sec².
